title: Finite transit durations raise conditional area floors by 1.8 to 2.8 times in 119 TESS CPVs at x=2
abstract: We test whether the finite duration of a transit adds an area constraint beyond a minimum equivalent width in 260 released TESS sectors of 119 complex periodic variables. We derive a positive interval relaxation for small isotropic cross sections on an equator-on corotating shell. A linear program fits broad stellar modulation and an unknown bare-star flux scale. At a shell radius of twice the stellar radius and a two-noise flux tolerance, the median area floor is 1.83 times the equivalent-width-only floor for two broad harmonics and 2.82 times for four. At three stellar radii, the factors are 1.40 and 1.90. At two radii the median effective zero-albedo absorption floors are 0.547% and 0.394%, respectively. All 2,080 shell fits pass primal and dual checks. Eighteen analytic tests and a flux-scale test pass. This is a conditional lower-bound method, not an attainable dust map or an infrared refit. Inclination, surface brightness, grain opacity and the Fourier baseline limit the physical inference. Code, aggregate results, figures and exact source hashes are included.

display.caption: Finite transit duration raises the area floor relative to a minimum equivalent width under the same baseline and error box. Bars are population quartiles, not confidence intervals.
Conditional shell area floors at two radii and two baseline choices. No infrared fit is performed.
